evidence.excerpt: The project develops and validates a suite of dynamic pricing models for small and medium-sized make-to-order job shops in Serbia, combining queueing-theoretic workload models with empirically estimated demand elasticity functions. Phase one collected order and capacity data from twelve partner firms and ran stated-preference surveys with their customers. Phase two developed and tested Bayesian learning pricing rules and lightweight surrogate models suitable for deployment in standard ERP environments. Phase three piloted pricing tools at four firms over six months and evaluated revenue and customer satisfaction outcomes. The project produced eight journal papers and one open-source pricing toolkit. Partners include industrial SMEs in the metalworking sector and one software firm supporting ERP customisation.
